fields.meta_description: Build a complaint form that gives every complainant a case number and routes each complaint to the person who can fix it.
fields.h1: Build a Complaint Form That Sends Every Case to Its Owner
fields.hero_description: Describe the complaints you receive and who handles each kind. Emergent builds the complaint form, gives every case a number and routes it by category or amount.
fields.features_heading: What a Complaint Needs After It Arrives
fields.features_subheading: The complaint forms that rank today are written for the person filing. These six pieces serve the team that has to answer.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the complaint type

Pick billing or delivery, and the next questions change to match. A billing complaint asks for the invoice and the amount charged, while a delivery one asks for the tracking number.
fields.feature_2:
A case number the moment it arrives

Email each complainant a case number and the date a reply is due. Staff search by that number when the person calls back, and the full history of the case opens on one screen.
fields.feature_3:
One owner for every complaint

Write the rules that decide who owns each case, such as routing by category or by the money at stake. Every complaint gets one named owner, plus a backup who covers days off.
fields.feature_4:
Reply targets with reminders

Give each category a reply target, such as two business days. Owners get a reminder the day before a target passes, and any case that goes past due turns red on the manager's list.
fields.feature_5:
Photos and receipts on the record

Let people attach photos or receipts before they submit. Each file stays on the case, and staff see the cracked base or the double charge without asking for it a second time.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub repository

Export the full codebase when the complaint log has to live inside a CRM or a city system. Your developers host it on your own servers and keep building on it from there.
fields.why_title: Why Build Complaint Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: An emailed complaint sits in a shared inbox until someone claims it. A complaint with an owner and a due date gets an answer.

fields.tab_content_1:
Any refund over $150 goes straight to Owen

Fernhill Home Goods sells lamps online, and most complaints are about damage in transit. A customer reports a cracked lamp with a photo and gets case 4471 by email. She asks for a $186 refund. Any refund request over $150 goes to Owen, the customer care lead, in Slack. Smaller ones wait in the support queue.
fields.tab_content_2:
Brookvale sorts every report by department

Brookvale residents used to phone city hall about a pothole and wait. Now they pick a category on the city's complaint page and give a street address. A streets complaint, such as a pothole on Alder Avenue, goes to Public Works. A barking dog goes to animal control. Each resident sees a reply due in 3 business days.
fields.tab_content_3:
Complaints about a manager skip that manager

Halden Freight drivers file complaints from the depot tablet, and each one normally goes to the driver's shift manager. When a Depot 2 driver names that shift manager, the app skips the manager and messages Monique, the HR director, directly. The manager sees nothing until HR decides what to share.
fields.tab_content_4:
One clinic owns most of the wait-time complaints

Patients at Riverbend Dental's four clinics file complaints on a checkout tablet. The practice manager sees them by clinic and category. This quarter brought 24 complaints about wait times, and 14 came from Elmwood. The chart flags Elmwood, and the manager books a scheduling review with its front desk.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Complaint Form
fields.howto_description: Decide who answers each kind of complaint before you write a single question.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask what the person wants done
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set a reply target per category
fields.howto_step_1_des: Sort the complaints you get into four or five categories, such as billing and delivery. Pull the last 50 from your inbox to check the split. Each category earns its own follow-up questions here and its own owner in step 3.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what happened and when, in the complainant's own words. Then ask what they want done, such as a refund or a callback. Owners who know the target before the first reply can close a case in fewer messages.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each category one owner. Then decide when a complaint should skip the usual path, for example when the amount at stake is large or when it names the person who would normally read it. Write those exceptions down before you build.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Base each category's reply target on what the complainant is waiting for. A double charge needs an answer by the next business day, while a note about store hours can wait a week. Post the targets where every owner can see them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your categories and owners into one prompt, with the reply targets beside them. Emergent builds the form and a complaints table, plus a dashboard by category. When a new category shows up next quarter, ask for it in a sentence and the form changes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the message people see after they submit. Include the case number, when to expect a reply and a phone number for anything urgent. A clear confirmation heads off the emails asking whether the complaint ever arrived.
fields.howto_step_7_des: File three test complaints from a phone, one for each route you set up. Check that each lands with the right owner, that the case number arrives by email and that photos open on the record. Delete the tests before you share the link.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is nine government and court pages: a Tenth Circuit PDF, attorney general consumer forms, a notarized mail-only judicial form, a city inquiry form and a police employee complaint form. Every one serves the person filing. Nobody in the top 10 serves the organization receiving complaints. This page answers what searchers ask about filing (the complainant, standing, deadlines, contacting the company first) and then shows four receivers what happens after submit: a store routing a refund over $150 to its care lead, a city sending each pothole or noise complaint to the department that fixes it, an HR team keeping a complaint away from the manager it names, and a dental group spotting one clinic behind most wait-time complaints.

claims_to_source: The person who files a complaint is called the complainant; in a civil lawsuit, the plaintiff
A civil action is commenced by filing a complaint with the court
To bring a case in federal court, a plaintiff must have standing: an injury caused by the defendant that a court can redress
A charge of employment discrimination generally must be filed with the EEOC within 180 calendar days, extended to 300 days where a state or local agency enforces a similar law
Consumers are advised to try to resolve a problem with the business first, then file with their state consumer protection office or attorney general
